title: I love Numo!
body: This is such a helpful app for people with ADHD! Not only is it a place to put all your thoughts together in a super helpful to-do list, but you can connect with other ADHDers, there are lessons to help manage your symptoms, places to ask questions about other people’s hacks and tips and tricks for getting through life Neurospicy! And all of it is gamified! You get points for adding to your to-do list, for finishing things on your to-do list, for taking a minute and checking in with yourself, for doing the lessons, and for posting in the chats! It gives my brain the dopamine boost it needs to help me get through my tasks! I love it!

author: JadeBouchard

title: Has potential
body: I love the interface and this app sets itself apart with its community. However, I strongly dislike how I have to pay to join any community. Lets be real - there’s always a free option to join an adhd community somewhere on Reddit, instagram, facebook, or WhatsApp. It would’ve been a great package for this to be an all-in-one app where it would help bring accountability while also having community support. Without the subscription, it functions like any other task app. I strongly believe there are other ways to monetize off this app in a way that won’t hinder the users from experiencing the unique features that set this app apart.

title: Time to say goodbye after 180+ days on this app.
body: 20$ per month is not cheap to pay for a faulty tasks check-off app. If you want to add mew features at least make sure the previous basic features keep working. The actual home page is so difficult to work with & keep having new bugs. All weekly scheduled task start showing on main page, scrolling doesn’t work, page gets stuck, it gets slow. When releasing new features at least run a smoke test on previous ones. I kept renewing subscription thinking it’s a startup, they are trying give them a chance.. but it’s not worth it. Plenty cheaper options in market which are not full of issues.

title: Taking advantage of ADHD
body: Paid $20 for the month and it offers absolutely nothing the included apps on an iPhone can’t do. The interface freezes if you try to mute or skip through the “mini lessons” which can be found in more depth online, for free. I suggest finding a good website or channel (YouTube, Instagram) that focuses on ADHD with life tips and hacks, buy a journal to take notes and then use a journal and clock to track tasks so you’re A) not wasting money on an app that should be less than $5 a month given the current (non existent) offerings, and B) not being dependent on the distracting, dopamine sucking phone
